trajectory_summary: The call opens with the customer leading — voicing a rooftop-placement objection before the rep gets through any verify — and the rep responds with direct, honest feasibility answers instead of scope-creep deflection. Energy dips through a long, disorganized bill-retrieval segment but the rep keeps the customer engaged by validating frustration at the utility rather than defending Ion, and the call closes with a specific day/time appointment. This is a customer-driven call that the rep successfully redirected into a booked outcome without over-promising on the elimination-of-bill claim.

observed_outcome.reasoning: Rep and customer agree on Thursday at 02:30 PM for a design/evaluation call, with the rep confirming 'Let's do 02:30' at 12:17 and PM clarified at 12:24. No spouse or co-owner was mentioned anywhere in the call.

bill_anchor_audit.bill_quote: about how much is your typical bill with them? $2.41.
bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captures the ~$241 bill figure but never explicitly ties it back as the customer's reason to move forward ('that's exactly the number solar would offset') — the conversation moves straight to bill-retrieval logistics instead. The flip should have landed right after the bill number was given, using it to reinforce the value of the design appointment.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: And what attracted me is I keep getting these advertisements that solar's free. The government pays for it.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The customer volunteers his interest trigger (free-solar advertisements) unprompted since the rep never explicitly asked 'what interested you in solar.' The rep corrects the misconception factually but never reconnects this ad-driven curiosity to the appointment value later in the call.

script_coverage.quote: Hi. This is Joe with Ion.
It's a brand new house with a brand new roof. It's only four months old.
Northneck or something, whatever it is.
about how much is your typical bill with them?
I had solar on my roof... through Sunrun Solar
if you happen to have a a utility bill handy, do you get them in the mail, or is it all online?
I can send you a a text message... to confirm that time.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: competitive-intel probe / objection inversion on prior-solar experience
primary_coaching_focus.quote: Yet, I still had a $63 electric bill from the electric company.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer volunteers a named competitor (Sunrun), a specific monthly figure, and an explicit trust concern in one breath. The rep answered honestly but didn't probe for details or flip the story toward the customer's own bill pain — this is a repeatable, coachable skill gap distinct from the mechanical bill-collection slog later in the call.

key_moments.quote: I don't I really don't wanna put anything on my roof.
key_moments.stewart_read: This opening line sets the entire arc of the call — a structural/placement objection raised before any verify has happened. The rep answers it factually (rooftop is standard, most cost-effective) but never flips it toward the customer's actual pain (why they want solar at all, i.e., the bill). This is the seed of every later re-litigation of the 'will my bill actually go down' question.

key_moments.quote: So we we just do the the rooftop solar. That's really the best spot for solar, and it's gonna be the most cost effective.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is closer-tier product/installation reasoning delivered directly to the customer at minute one, before any qualification. It's a defensible, honest answer to a legitimate feasibility gate rather than a technical spec debate, so the scope-creep risk here is low.

key_moments.quote: Yet, I still had a $63 electric bill from the electric company.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior Ion-competitor (Sunrun) experience where the bill was NOT eliminated, directly challenging the rep's claim. The rep responds honestly ('sometimes we're not able to offset it a 100%') but never inverts this into the customer's Northneck bill pain as the reason to still move forward, nor probes competitive intel on the Sunrun deal.

key_moments.quote: Yet, I still had a $63 electric bill from the electric company.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer names a specific prior installer (Sunrun) and a specific monthly figure ($250 solar bill). This is a competitive-intel goldmine the rep let pass without a follow-up question about what happened, why he left it behind, or what the actual system size/state was.
